skill.name: create-feature
skill.description: Coordinates feature development from requirements analysis through backend work, frontend work, quality checks, and pull request creation.
skill.summary: Runs an ordered feature delivery workflow with specialist skills and quality gates.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: All static Ruby or shell backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or inline documentation paths. The high-entropy heuristic is also a false positive because SKILL.md is plain Markdown text. A semantic concern remains because the workflow can automate repository changes and pull request creation without an explicit approval gate.

remediation.issue: Autonomous pull request creation without an approval checkpoint
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit user confirmation before branch creation, repository modifications, commits, and pull request creation.
Document that companion skills may edit files, run tests, access Figma or Context7, and require GitHub permissions.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static command scanners
remediation.suggestion: Label command examples as documentation and avoid unnecessary fenced shell blocks when plain prose is sufficient.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Repository Changes and PR Creation
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs end-to-end feature work, GitHub pull request creation, and completion without human intervention except errors. This can change repository state and publish PRs without an explicit approval checkpoint.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly describe PR creation and complete automation. This is an operational security concern, but there is no evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Feature delivery often requires analysis, backend work, frontend work, reviews, tests, and PR creation. This skill guides that sequence with specialist skill calls and quality gates.
actual_capabilities: Collects feature name, issue number, optional specification path, Figma URL, and target scope.
Creates or verifies a feature branch before implementation.
Calls requirement analysis, backend, frontend, architecture review, QA, and PR creation skills in sequence.
Routes backend, frontend, or full stack implementation based on the target parameter.
Requires review, QA, 80 percent coverage, lint, tests, and build success before completion.
Produces a final completion report with implemented work, tests, coverage, and PR URL.
limitations: It depends on companion skills that are not included in this package.
It cannot guarantee GitHub authentication or repository permissions.
It may need user input when external resources, builds, or tests fail.
It does not validate business requirements beyond the provided specification and project context.

use_cases.title: Build a Backend Feature
use_cases.description: Coordinate requirements analysis, data model work, service code, API updates, tests, and backend quality checks.

use_cases.title: Ship a Full Stack Flow
use_cases.description: Run backend and frontend implementation in one ordered workflow with shared issue tracking and review gates.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Reviewable Pull Request
use_cases.description: Move a completed feature through architecture review, QA checks, completion reporting, and PR creation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Backend Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-feature for feature_name="user profile" issue_number=123 target="backend". Use the specification at docs/user-profile.md.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Frontend Feature from Figma
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-feature for feature_name="settings page" issue_number=234 target="frontend". Use this Figma URL and the provided specification path.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Stack Feature Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-feature for feature_name="team invitations" issue_number=345 target="fullstack". Analyze requirements first, then implement both layers.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and Complete a Failed Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-feature for feature_name="billing alerts" issue_number=456 target="fullstack". Fix review or QA failures until the workflow passes.

output_examples.input: A backend-only feature request with an issue number and specification path.
output_examples.output: A branch check, requirements analysis, backend implementation summary, test results, coverage status, and PR link.

output_examples.input: A frontend feature request with a Figma URL.
output_examples.output: A frontend implementation summary with page components, container components, tests, Storybook notes, QA results, and PR status.

output_examples.input: A full stack feature request that fails QA on the first pass.
output_examples.output: A failure summary, targeted fixes, repeated QA execution, final quality results, and completion report.

best_practices: Provide a clear feature name, issue number, target scope, and specification path before starting.
Review generated changes before allowing commits or pull request creation.
Confirm companion skills and project documentation exist in the repository.
anti_patterns: Do not use it without a valid issue number or branch strategy.
Do not skip human review for sensitive, financial, authentication, or permission changes.
Do not run it when required companion skills are missing or untrusted.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: Yes. It delegates backend and frontend implementation to companion skills when the target requires them.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on analyze-requirements, develop-backend, develop-frontend, review-architecture, qa-check, and create-pr.

faq.question: Can it work without a GitHub issue?
faq.answer: No. The workflow expects one issue number for branch naming, skill calls, and PR creation.

faq.question: Does it support backend-only work?
faq.answer: Yes. Set target to backend to skip frontend implementation.

faq.question: Does it use Figma?
faq.answer: It can pass a Figma URL to requirement analysis and frontend work when one is provided.

faq.question: What checks happen before completion?
faq.answer: It requires architecture review, QA checks, tests, lint, build verification, and at least 80 percent coverage.
